# Internal-information denylist for the full-history scan (ci.yml → provenance job).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#   This repository is a public sample derived from an internal one. A previous
#   publication attempt copied the internal baseline first and sanitized it in a
#   follow-up commit — which left the original text permanently readable in git
#   history even though HEAD looked clean. Scanning HEAD only cannot catch that.
#   The provenance job therefore scans EVERY blob reachable from EVERY ref.
#
# SELF-REFERENCE TRAP (read this before editing)
#   A denylist that literally spells a forbidden word would match itself and
#   fail the build forever. Excluding this file by path is not reliable either:
#   a blob can appear under a different path elsewhere in history. So every
#   pattern below is written so that it does NOT literally contain the string it
#   matches — exactly one character is wrapped in a character class, e.g. a
#   pattern of the form  Xxxx[y]yyy  matches Xxxxyyyy without spelling it.
#   THIS APPLIES TO COMMENTS TOO: never write a forbidden word in prose here.
#   Verify after every edit — the following must print nothing:
#       PATF=$(mktemp); sed -e 's/#.*//' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' \
#         .github/internal-terms.txt > "$PATF"
#       grep -inE -f "$PATF" .github/internal-terms.txt
#
# FORMAT
#   One POSIX extended regex (ERE) per line. Blank lines and #-comments are
#   ignored. Matching is case-insensitive.

# ── Enterprise device-compliance / identity plumbing ──────────────────────────
# These name internal components, and an earlier revision of this repo went
# further: it documented a step-by-step way to make them work under a
# non-standard browser profile. Neither the names nor the procedure belong here.
# Note: the first pattern below already covers any string containing it, so
# hostname variants of it do not need their own entries.
[M]idway
\bA[E]A\b
\bAC[M]E\b
\bacme[d]\b
Yubi[K]ey
idpris[m]
amazon_enterprise_[a]ccess
NativeMessaging[H]osts
# Chrome extension ID of the enterprise-access extension. Never publish an
# internal extension ID — it is a stable identifier that ties this public repo
# to internal browser tooling.
bkbighdlgofgdhcjnhocalbkiehhpde[i]

# ── Internal infrastructure identifiers ───────────────────────────────────────
# Account / org / group names leak deployment topology. The start URL must be
# built from QUICK_WEB_ACCOUNT / QUICK_WEB_BASE, never a hardcoded real account.
amazon[b]i
gitlab\.aws\.[d]ev
aws-gcr-[w]eb3

# ── Customer / engagement identity (highest business impact) ──────────────────
# Real Space names identify customers. In docs and examples use a placeholder
# such as  <Customer>  followed by a generic suffix — never a real account's
# Space name, and never a real customer name in a sample command line.
Rock[b]und
Client [3]60
Field [T]ools
Account [P]lanning
Transformation-in-[F]inance

# ── NOT scanned here: product-internal API names ──────────────────────────────
# Those live in .github/internal-terms-head-only.txt and are checked against the
# working tree only. Reason (a hard constraint, not a preference): one such name
# is frozen into refs/pull/1/head, whose source branch no longer exists. A PR ref
# follows its branch only while the branch lives; once the branch is deleted the
# ref — and every commit it reaches — can never be rewritten. Listing that term
# here would make this job permanently red with no possible remedy, which is the
# fastest way to get a security gate deleted by whoever hits it next.
# LESSON: rewrite history BEFORE any PR branch referencing it disappears.
